land.text: the east of Hispaniola, 'Spanish Haiti' annexed by Haiti in February 1822 and held for 'twenty-two years'; the Dominicans 'declared independence from Haiti' on 27 February 1844

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Empire of Haiti shape of 1822-1845 holds the whole island; the Haiti dossier (slug haiti) carries both Names.

capitals.name: Santo Domingo
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital and largest city'. The seat of the Restoration government of 1863-1865 and the Spanish governor-general of 1861-1865 are not stated by the pages opened.

correction.text: the 1846 shape (the eastern part of Hispaniola, the present Dominican Republic) held for 1844-1845: on 27 February 1844 'some 100 Dominicans seized the fortress' at Santo Domingo and the Haitian garrison surrendered on 28 February

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria draws all the island as Haitian until 1845 and starts the Dominican row in 1846. Haitian forces nevertheless occupied Azua after 19 March 1844 and invaded again in 1845 and 1849, so the border is contested (ledger).

52,641 km2 against the infobox's 48,671 km2 (ratio 1.08); the same outline is used for every year, though the page says the Haitian frontier 'was not finalized until 1936' and the shape overlaps Cliopatria's Haiti shape by 9 cells (about 2,276 km2) along the border. Infobox 'First Republic: 1844-1861' fits the end of this shape in 1860; the annexation to Spain is a ledger loss in 1861.

52,641 km2 (ratio 1.08); the Restoration War ended with Spain's departure ('By July 15, there were no more Spanish troops left on the island') and the infobox's 'Second Republic: 1865-1916'. Cliopatria's gap 1861-1864 is the Spanish annexation: its Spanish Empire shape covers the whole country in those years (and still in 1865), which the ledger records as a loss, a contest and a gain.

correction.text: the 1924 shape (same outline) held for 1916-1923 as Dominican land occupied by the United States: 'U.S. Marines landed on May 16, 1916, and seized the capital and other ports'; the US military government began on 29 November (1916); control returned to Dominican hands with Vásquez's inauguration on 13 July 1924

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria draws the Dominican Republic as United States land in 1916-1923 (its US shape covers the whole country, 251 cells), but the page has an occupation under a military government (infobox 'Third Republic: 1924-1965' resumes in 1924), not an annexation, so the country stays Dominican and hatched (occupation events). The page gives 'the U.S. government's rule ended in October 1922' (Vicini Burgos provisional president 21 October 1922) and the last US forces left in September 1924 (Dominican Republic page).

52,641 km2 (ratio 1.08 to the infobox). The frontier with Haiti was agreed in 1929, a treaty of 27 February 1935 allocated the sections in dispute and the final border treaty was signed on 9 March 1936 (border page); the constant outline cannot show the four towns the Dominican Republic gave up.

region.text: the former Spanish colony in the east of Hispaniola, held by Haiti from February 1822

ledger.note: 1844: La Trinitaria declares the Dominican Republic independent of Haiti. 'On February 27, 1844, some 100 Dominicans seized the fortress of' Puerta del Conde; the Haitian garrison surrendered on 28 February. First constitution adopted 6 November 1844 (Dominican Republic page).

region.text: the Haitian frontier country: Azua in the south, Santiago in the north, Las Carreras, Sabana Larga

ledger.note: 1844: Haiti invades to retake the east. 'After Santana's victory at the Battle of Azua on March 19,' Santana withdrew and Haitian forces occupied Azua; the Dominicans beat the Haitians at Santiago on 30 March and sank three Haitian ships on 15 April. Further invasions followed on 6 August 1845, 9 March 1849 (Las Carreras, 21-22 April 1849) and November 1855. The frontier band is the researcher's reading of where the fighting was.

region.text: the Haitian frontier country: Azua in the south, Santiago in the north, Las Carreras, Sabana Larga

ledger.note: 1856: the last Haitian invasion fails at Sabana Larga. The war 'ended on January 24, 1856' (infobox '27 February 1844 - 24 January 1856'; the text dates Sabana Larga to 27 January). Haiti 'finally recognized its independence in 1867'.

region.text: the whole republic: 'Spain ... annexed the country'; 'Santana asked Queen Isabella II of Spain to retake control'

ledger.note: 1861: Santana hands the republic to Spain. 'On March 18, 1861, the annexation was announced' and Santana became Governor-General of the new province (infobox 'First Republic: 1844-1861'); Contreras's rebellion on 2 May 1861 failed.

region.text: the whole country: the Capotillo raid and the rebel government in the Cibao against Spanish-held ports and the south

ledger.note: 1863: the Restoration War begins. 'The war began on August 16, 1863' with a raid on Capotillo; the rebels besieged Fort San Luis at Santiago on 3 September and the Spanish garrison 'evacuated the fort on September 13'; the page does not draw the territory held by either side, so the whole country is the zone.

region.text: the whole country, cleared of Spanish troops

ledger.note: 1865: Spain leaves the island. Queen Isabella II 'signed the annulment of the annexation' on 3 March 1865 and 'By July 15, there were no more Spanish troops left on the island' (infobox 'Date: 16 August 1863 - 15 July 1865').
1865: the Dominican Republic is restored. Infobox result Dominican victory, with restoration of sovereignty, Spanish withdrawal and the establishment of the Second Republic.

region.text: the whole republic: Marines 'claimed to have restored order throughout most of the republic, with the exception of the eastern region' (El Seibo and San Pedro de Macorís)

ledger.note: 1916: United States Marines occupy the Dominican Republic. Santo Domingo was occupied on 15 May 1916 (infobox 5 May 1916 - 27 December 1924) and 'on the 29 November the United States imposed a military government under Captain (later Rear Admiral) Harry Shepard Knapp'. Hughes-Peynado agreement of 30 June 1922; Vicini Burgos provisional president from 21 October 1922.

1924: control returns to the Dominicans. After the election of 15 March 1924, 'With his inauguration on July 13, control of the republic returned to Dominican hands'; the Dominican Republic page has the last US forces leaving in September, and the customs convention of 27 December 1924 ran to 1941.
1924: the Third Republic. Infobox 'Third Republic: 1924-1965'; Horacio Vásquez inaugurated 13 July 1924. The state and its colour continue (First Republic 1844-1861, Second Republic 1865-1916).

region.text: the central border towns of Hinche, Las Caobas, San Miguel de la Atalaya and San Rafael de la Angostura on the Haitian side, whose claims the Dominican Republic 'formally relinquished' in 1936; drawn as a 45 km radius around Hinche outside the Dominican Republic

ledger.note: 1936: the frontier with Haiti is finalized. The border page: 'a final border treaty being signed on 9 March 1936' after the treaty of 27 February 1935 allocated the sections still in dispute; the War of Independence page: the frontier 'was not finalized until 1936', when the Dominican Republic formally relinquished its claims to the central border towns of Hinche, Las Caobas, San Miguel de la Atalaya and San Rafael de la Angostura. The towns lie on the Haitian side of Cliopatria's constant outline, so the event records a renounced claim and moves no Dominican cell (the region was a border band, which would have cut the Dominican side of the frontier) (reviewer am-08-f).
1966: the Fourth Republic. Infobox 'Fourth Republic: 1966-present', after the civil war of April 1965 and the second American occupation. The state and its colour continue.

wars.name: Dominican War of Independence
wars.outcome: Dominican victory: Haitian garrison surrendered at Santo Domingo on 28 February 1844; invasions of 1845, 1849 and 1855-56 were defeated; 'ended on January 24, 1856'; Haiti recognised independence in 1867; a mediated truce came in 1851 (UK, France, US).
wars.note: The page's text and its battle table disagree on the dates of Beler (27 September or 27 November 1845) and Sabana Larga (27 or 24 January 1856).

wars.name: Dominican Restoration War
wars.outcome: Dominican victory: 16 August 1863 - 15 July 1865; Spain annulled the annexation on 3 March 1865 and left the island; the Second Republic followed.
wars.note: Spanish forces took Azua, Baní, Barahona and Monte Cristi in December 1863 and May 1864; the rebels held Santiago from 13 September 1863; no territorial extents are given.

wars.name: United States occupation of the Dominican Republic (1916-1924)
wars.outcome: Marines landed in May 1916 and a US military government ruled from 29 November 1916; Dominican control returned on 13 July 1924; the customs convention of 27 December 1924 gave the US control of customs revenue.
wars.note: Treated as an occupation, not an annexation; Cliopatria draws the country as United States land.

wars.name: Dominican Civil War (1965)
wars.outcome: A coup of 24 April 1965 ousted Donald Reid Cabral; President Johnson sent Marines to Santo Domingo on 28 April; the Fourth Republic dates from 1966.
wars.note: No ledger occupation is recorded because the pages opened give no end of the second American occupation.

certainty.note: The border with Haiti was 'not finalized until 1936' (a more precise line had been drawn in 1777 and a treaty followed in 1929); the Dominican state is also absent 1861-1864 and under occupation 1916-1924.
'A final border treaty being signed on 9 March 1936'; the border is 376-392 km long (the pages differ).

notes: Pages: five (budget). Cliopatria's four shapes are one outline (52,641 km2); the gaps 1861-1864 (Spanish Empire row) and 1916-1923 (United States row) are the annexation and the occupation. The Restoration government of 1863-1865 is treated as the Dominican Republic itself, not as a rebel state (it claimed to be the Republic; the pages do not name its seat). Not settled with the pages opened: which four border towns were given up in 1936; the territory each side held in 1863-1865; the end of the 1965-66 American occupation; whether Cliopatria's Empire of Haiti shape (which overlaps this one by 2,276 km2) or this one is right on the border. The haiti dossier (slug haiti) ends in 1935 and republic-of-haiti begins in 1936: the 1936 loss uses republic-of-haiti. Dates differ between pages: the war of independence ended 24 or 27 January 1856; the last US forces left in September 1924 (Dominican Republic page) or control returned on 13 July 1924 (occupation page). Gazetteer: no new names.
